topic: The hidden economics of $6 AI agents
angle: If you don’t meter agent work at the task level, your ROI is imaginary—and costs leak at night.
sourceTitle: 🔮 The curious economics of a $6 AI agent #597
linkedinPost:
AI spend doesn’t explode. It evaporates—quietly.

Exponential View shared a wild anecdote: an AI agent project ran for months, racking up charges while no one noticed. The headline number was “$6,” but the real story is invisible usage and missing unit economics.

Here’s the enterprise pattern I see: teams meter models, not work. Without task-level accounting, you can’t tell if a $0.03 call saved $30 of labor—or spawned 300 more calls at 2 a.m.

Fix it with three moves: give every agent a unique identity and budget, meter per task (ticket resolved, lead qualified, claim drafted), and enforce guardrails (sandbox, max steps, and an auto-off switch on anomalies). Your dashboard should show cost-per-outcome, not tokens burned.

Then price the outcome: if an agent drafts a response that cuts handle time by 45 seconds, attribute the labor delta. If it escalates, charge the rework back to the agent’s P&L.

If you can’t meter it, you can’t manage it—and you definitely can’t scale it.

What’s the one outcome metric you’ll tie to every agent before year-end? #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #AIStrategy
